rationale: Version 12 (registered 2026-11-19, before any model read heldout-dev-v0.8.21; docs/records/evals/2026-11-19-release-requirements-v12.md) adds a development collection and keeps every other v11 value: each requirement, the objective, the statistics, the provenance rule, the scorer, the inference rule, the published identity, the confirmation role and identities.dataset. The candidate identity stays null; a candidate that passes the development role is registered by v13. Why: under the text-matching overlap audit (overlap.run.ts --match-text) v11's development role leaves few comparison rows: graded against the v0.8.20 corpus, heldout-dev-v0.8.18 keeps 426 US rows, and v8.7.0 seed 42 and v8.8.0 seed 42 both read insufficient evidence on geocode and the objective. heldout-dev-v0.8.21@7f9dcfb6572d4bf9 holds 44,978 rows in 44,060 groups and 16 countries, frozen by freeze.run.ts with seed 1827 at 4,000 rows per country and kind from the test split of corpus v0.8.18-retention-overlay (MANIFEST.json sha256 2241efda2892634dc8b4b50ceddef6708680b95adf38055f2ae020a5d236a9d0), the rows 10.8.0 held out, with every read or registered collection excluded (heldout-dev-v0.8.18 v4 as sampling.excludes, 22 more under sampling.excludesRead, among them both confirmation collections, the IN supplement and every probe set). Its 10.8.0 audit with --match-text (heldout-dev-v0.8.21.provenance-10.8.0.json) classes 35,084 rows verified_unseen and 9,894 known_overlap; every US and FR overlap is a group another rendering of which 10.8.0 trained on. Its verified_unseen ordinary address groups: US 96, FR 193, DE 3,038, ES 3,756, IT 3,987, AU 730 (the whole AU pool), and GB, IN and NZ 0: the earlier collections took every test group of those three countries. heldout-dev-v0.8.18 therefore stays in the role for GB, IN and NZ, with heldout-dev-v0.8.19-probes-r2 for the capability probes. The three collections share no group. A candidate trained on corpus v0.8.21 never sees heldout-dev-v0.8.21, because evaluation-groups.v0.8.21.json lists its groups (heldout-dev-v0.8.21.groups.json) and the v0.8.21 re-split sends them to test. v8.7.0 seeds 42 and 43 and v8.8.0 trained on these rows, so the new collection grades no earlier arm. No model has read heldout-dev-v0.8.21. Reads of v11: its development role was read on 2026-11-19 by 10.8.0, v8.7.0 seed 42 and v8.8.0 seed 42 (lane AR, /mnt/mw/models/arms/v880/); no model read its confirmation role.

requirements.task: Reading a PO Box, locked bag or CEDEX designator as one component beside an intact locality line
requirements.reason: Closed-vocabulary slot behind the former us.po_box_real and fr.cedex_real floors.
requirements.maxLossReason: A closed-vocabulary slot that moves 5 pp has lost a surface form; the country minima would absorb a loss this size.

requirements.task: Recovering a venue name and its unit designator ahead of the street line
requirements.reason: The former us.unit_real floor (n=34) on the one held-out source with a controlled unit span (1,936 rows).

requirements.task: A trailing country name tagged country rather than absorbed into the locality
requirements.reason: The former us.country_homograph_f1 floor (n=54) protected the country slot; the homograph confound stays a diagnostic.

requirements.task: Reading a flat, unit, floor, staircase or building designator with its identifier as one unit component, in the line position the postal operator's guideline gives it
requirements.reason: Issue #2764: cited operator rules for FR (SP 8855 lines 2 and 3), GB (PAF Sub Building Name), IT (scala, piano, interno on line 3), AU (FLAT/UNIT TYPE table) and NZ (ADV358 Unit Type), with only designators no training recipe draws. A row whose expected spans hold a venue is left out: the FR named complexes (RESIDENCE, LOTISSEMENT), labeled venue since recipe fix 48fca721dd, carry no unit span, so they don't test this task.
requirements.maxLossReason: The operator decided on 2026-11-18 that a release mustn't lose this capability against the published model, which reads it below any registered minimum: no training recipe draws these designators, so the rate a candidate reaches measures the corpus, and the release decides only whether the change loses it. No loss is the objective's own threshold (minimumImprovement 0), so an arm whose difference interval reaches below zero reads insufficient evidence, as the objective does.

requirements.task: Resolving an ordinary address to the components and admin places its answer key gives, on the geocode path production runs
requirements.reason: A change that acts only in the resolver, such as countyDesignatorFallback, leaves every exact-parse outcome equal, so no other check can judge it (lane Y, docs/records/evals/2026-11-17-county-fallback-and-arabic-fold.md). The outcome is heldout/per/geocode-outcome's: the resolved components and every written locality, dependent locality, subregion, region and country placed at its tag.
requirements.maxLossReason: The objective admits no exact-parse loss in the equal-country rate (minimumImprovement 0). The geocode outcome is bounded at one point of the same equal-country rate. A model change reads the comparative rows, so the bound inherits the objective's width; a resolver change, with one model in both arms, reads every recorded class and its bound decides at one point.

inference.description: HELDOUT_INFERENCE_RULE in heldout/per/country.ts (served-locale-package): each row is parsed by the shipped Latin locale package for its country (release.config.json locales), falling back to en-us, with the row's country as localeHint; a package whose loader reports an unfed required channel is refused. The verdict records the rule and the rows each package parsed.

statistics.groupingAssumption: A row's independent unit is its group within its country: base_source_id when derived, else source_id. Rows are not declared independent, so a check that reads an ungrouped row is insufficient evidence. Limitation: structure shared across groups (one source's conventions, one place's many addresses) is not modelled. The dataset quota counts groups, not rows, against 1,000 per country.
